PROCEDURE
Preparation of 100 ml of —
- oxalic acid solution
A. Accurately weigh out about 0.63 gm of oxalic acid crystals by placing I. them on a watch glass. Note the weight taken.

Transfer all the particles of oxalic acid crystals into the volumetric flask quantitatively with the help of the funnel. Wash down the particles left on the watch glass with the help of the distilled water.
Dissolve the crystals with a little distilled water. The solution should not splash while dissolving the solute.
Then add distilled water upto the neck of the flask through the funnel.
Remove the funnel and add more water dropwisely with the help of a pipette so that the lower meniscus of the soluåon coincides the mark of the volumetric flask.
Close the flask with its lid and shake the solution.

Clean the burette with distilled water and rinse it with the standard solution of the acid.
Clamp the burette vertically to the stand so that the jet of the bUrette remains slightly above the mouth of the conical flask. Fill the bUrette with acid upto the zero mark.
Clean the pipette with distilled water and rinse it with the given NaOH solution.
Pipette out 10 ml of the given alkali into a conical flask. Add 2-3 drops of phenolphthalein and shake gently.

Take the first reading by running out 1 ml of the acid at a time from the burette into the alkali taken in the conical flask. Shake the flask during each addition giving the rotatory motion to the solution into the flask.
When the pink colour just disappears, end point is attained. Note the volume of the acid in the burette.
Wash the conical flask. Repeat the procedure and take some more readings till you get at least two concurrent readings.
